metaData.title: AI Agent Collaborative Operations at Sina Weibo: Implementation and Evolution
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Sina Weibo shares its practical experience in deploying AI Agents for operations, leveraging knowledge bases, MCP tools, and a layered AI system to significantly improve efficiency in scenarios such as hot event response and root cause analysis.
metaData.summary: This article is a compilation of a speech by Ma Zhen, head of the basic platform at Sina Weibo's R&D center, at a technology conference. It provides a detailed introduction to the overall approach and implementation cases of AI Agent collaborative operations at Weibo. It first analyzes the escalating complexity of operations brought by cloud-native and multi-cloud environments, as well as the limitations of traditional AIOps such as data silos, loss of experience, and high human-machine interaction barriers. It then proposes a three-step strategy: AI-assisted programming, foundational capability building (operations knowledge base and MCP tool encapsulation), and AI Agent construction. It highlights three representative scenarios — Hot Event Response AI Agent, Root Cause Analysis Public Opinion Agent, and Client Crash Analysis — each outlining the pain points of traditional methods and the significant improvements brought by AI solutions. Finally, it summarizes insights from the implementation: not all scenarios require large models, importance of data cleaning and cost control, human-machine collaboration to address hallucinations, and assistance from smaller models. Overall, it presents a capability layering of AI + AIOps (AI-assisted development, foundational capability base, and AI Agent-assisted decision-making), offering a reference path for operations teams of similar scale.

mainPoints.point: Traditional AIOps has clear limitations in data silos, loss of experience, human-machine interaction barriers, and generalization of single-point models.
mainPoints.explanation: Cloud-native and microservices have increased the number of services to over 3,000 and monitoring items to tens of millions, making it difficult for traditional models to meet the "1, 5, 10" service level objectives, making an upgrade imperative.

mainPoints.point: Sina Weibo's AI system is built in three major steps and five key phases: AI-assisted programming, foundational capability building, and AI Agent construction.
mainPoints.explanation: First, improve ops development efficiency through AI-assisted programming; then build a knowledge base and MCP tools as foundational capabilities; finally, gradually transform high-frequency scenarios into AI Agents to form a tool matrix.

mainPoints.point: Hot event response, root cause analysis, and client crash analysis are the three AI Agent scenarios with the most significant implementation results.
mainPoints.explanation: The AI Agent automatically collects data, aggregates analysis, and outputs hot event summaries, traffic characteristics, root cause localization, and handling recommendations, greatly reducing response time. Traditional manual methods are inefficient and rely on personal experience.

mainPoints.point: Implementation experience emphasizes "not all scenarios need large models," introducing AI-enhanced mechanisms, data cleaning, human-machine collaboration, and small model assistance.
mainPoints.explanation: In some scenarios, using AI to optimize automation strategies is more efficient and cost-effective; destructive operations require human-machine confirmation; small models can handle annotation tasks to balance efficiency and cost.

mainPoints.point: AI + AIOps capabilities should be divided into three layers: AI-assisted development, foundational capability base, and AI Agent-assisted decision-making.
mainPoints.explanation: The bottom layer is AI-assisted coding to improve development efficiency; the middle layer is the knowledge base and MCP tool API system; the top layer is Agent-assisted decision-making and enhanced automation, forming a complete intelligent operations system.

keyQuotes: Lesson one: not all scenarios need to use large models.
The vast majority of problems (over 90%) are caused by changes — no change, no failure.
Human-machine collaboration to address hallucinations: when destructive operations are involved, introduce a human-machine collaboration mechanism and add a confirmation step to ensure safety.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Stop Manual Log Checking: Diagnose Bugs with AI + MCP in One Click
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to automate the fixed workflow of log querying, code analysis, and root cause localization using the MCP protocol and Claude Code Skill, enabling one-click bug diagnosis.

relatedArticles.title: A True Agent Must Remember! The Memory Architecture and Thinking That Tens of Thousands of Words Can't Fully Explain
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically proposes the core architecture of an Agent memory system, abstracting Memory into a trio of Raw Ledger, Views, and Policy, and delves into cutting-edge directions such as temporal memory, procedural memory, and the memory integration layer.

relatedArticles.title: Rethinking the AI Revolution: Has Software Engineering Ever Truly Been "Engineered" in the Past 50 Years?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: From an engineering philosophy perspective, this article argues that software engineering has not truly been engineered in the past five decades. It posits that large language models (LLMs) have, for the first time, achieved "exchanging energy for high-level intelligence," marking the true arrival of software engineering. It systematically deduces a new AI-centric paradigm, implementation pathways, and the evolution of human roles.

relatedArticles.title: Redefining Skill Development: A Step-by-Step Guide & One-Stop Development Assistant Launch
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces the concept of AI Agent Skill, including its directory structure, writing standards, release process, and cross-platform challenges. It also launches a one-stop Skill development assistant, skill-dev-aio, designed to free developers from tedious tool learning and allow them to focus on experience and judgment.

relatedArticles.title: Stop Idolizing RAG! Grep Makes a Comeback, Vector Indexing Becomes a Fallback?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article dissects the technical architecture of Claude Code, which abandons RAG and vector indexing in favor of LLM-driven Grep for code search, demonstrating that in code search scenarios, a zero-index Grep approach outperforms traditional embedding retrieval in both efficiency and effectiveness.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: No More Manual SQL for Data Validation! Complete Design Review of Alibaba's Production-Grade End-to-End Agent Skill
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a detailed review of the design of Alibaba's production-grade data validation Agent Skill (verify-data), covering the full workflow from natural language trigger to automatically generating validation SQL, executing it, and producing reports, including architecture, core capabilities, real-world cases, design principles, and lessons learned.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Harness Engineering: Finding the Shell That Keeps AI from Going Rogue—Insights from 14 Engineering Articles | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of "Harness Engineering," a core technology in the AI Agent field. It reveals how to compensate for model shortcomings through a three-layer management architecture and proposes the logic of "Compensation Surface Migration" that evolves with model capabilities.
